w:r.w:t: The Diagnostic Engine is the entry gate for every new student on TestCrack. Before a student can access any practice module, the system must establish a baseline band score across all four IELTS skills. This baseline drives everything downstream: the level assignment (A/B/C), the content that is unlocked, and the first batch of suggestions generated by the recommendation engine.

Without a completed diagnostic, the student sees a locked dashboard. The diagnostic cannot be skipped. This document describes exactly how the engine works, how the frontend must render and respond to each state
Why this matters to the product

The diagnostic is the first impression. A student who completes the 10-minute gate and immediately sees their band scores, their level badge, and three targeted suggestions will trust the platform. A student who lands on a blank dashboard with no context will leave. Get this right before anything else.
The engine is made up of four components working in sequence.
owns the Scoring Service and the Matrix Writer. The Recommendation Seed is a shared boundary.

Each diagnostic run also writes one row per skill to assessment_history with columns: id, student_id, skill, mode (diagnostic | practice | mock), band_score, sub_scores, feedback_json, transcript (Speaking only), created_at.
The level badge displayed to the student (A, B, or C) is derived from the band score returned by the scoring service.

Every screen in the diagnostic flow has multiple states.
must implement all of them — missing a state causes blank screens or frozen UIs that break user trust.
idle — student has not yet started. Show CTA, estimated time (10 minutes), and brief description of what the test covers.
in_progress — student already started but closed the app. Show 'Resume diagnostic' CTA with the phase they were on.
complete — diagnostic already done. Redirect to Dashboard immediately. Do not show the gate again.
loading — API call to fetch questions is in flight. Show skeleton loader, never a blank screen.
ready — questions loaded. Enable interaction. Timer starts (if applicable).
submitting — student has submitted. Disable all inputs. Show loading indicator on submit button.
scoring — backend is scoring. Show spinner with contextual message (differs for AI vs. rule-based scoring).
scored — result received. Show interim result card before moving to next section.
error — API call failed. Show error message with retry option. Do not lose student's answers — keep them in local state.
idle — ready to record. Tap to start.
recording — waveform animation playing. Timer counting up. 'Tap to stop' label.
recorded — recording stopped. Audio playback control available (optional at MVP). 'Submit' CTA enabled.
uploading — file uploading to backend. Spinner. Prevent double-tap.
processing — Whisper + Claude pipeline running. 'Transcribing...' message.
done — scores returned. Transition to SpeakingResultCard.
pending — not all 4 skills scored yet. Should not be reachable, but show a safe loading state if hit.
ready — all scores present. Show band cards for all 4 skills, level badge, and 'Go to dashboard' CTA.

A task is complete when: (a) the screen/component renders without errors in the dev build, (b) all states listed in Section 4 are handled, (c) the API call uses the exact request/response shape from Section 5, and (d) Paul has reviewed it on the staging environment.

Build the full-screen blocker that appears for new students. Must check diagnostic_complete flag on student profile. If false, render gate with 'Start diagnostic' CTA. If true, redirect to Dashboard silently.
New student sees gate. Returning student with diagnostic_complete = true never sees it.

Render 6 MCQ questions with a single-play audio player above them. Audio uses the URL returned by the questions API. Track selected answers in local state. Show question counter. Enable Submit only when all 6 answered.
All 6 questions render. Audio plays once. Answers tracked. Submit calls POST /api/diagnostic/submit-section with skill: 'listening'.

Render a 200-word passage above 4 True/False/Not Given questions. Radio button selection per question. Soft 5-minute timer displayed (non-blocking — student can still submit after time). Enable Submit when all 4 answered.
Passage and questions render. Timer counts down. Submit calls POST /api/diagnostic/submit-section with skill: 'reading'.

Display a graph image (provided by backend as URL) with the writing prompt text below it. Textarea with live word count. Submit disabled until word count >= 60. On submit, show 'AI is evaluating...' spinner for up to 20 seconds while awaiting response.
Word count updates live. Submit calls POST /api/diagnostic/submit-writing. Spinner shown during wait. Writing band score displayed on return.

Build RecordButton component with all states from Section 4.3. Use browser MediaRecorder API to capture audio. Output format: webm (preferred) or mp4. Show animated bar or waveform during recording. Auto-stop at 90 seconds. Upload via multipart form to POST /api/diagnostic/submit-speaking.
Recording starts, stops, and uploads without errors. All 6 states (idle, recording, recorded, uploading, processing, done) render correctly. Audio duration <= 90 seconds enforced.

After each section is scored, render an interim result card before showing the next section CTA. Card shows: skill name, band score (large), level badge (A/B/C derived client-side from band score per Section 2.3), and one sentence of encouragement.
Card renders after each of the 4 skills. Level badge colour: A = amber, B = indigo, C = teal. 'Continue' CTA advances to next section.

Final screen in the diagnostic flow. Show all 4 skill band scores as cards in a 2x2 grid, the overall level badge (derived from average band score), a congratulations message, and a 'Go to dashboard' CTA that navigates to the main dashboard and sets diagnostic_complete = true on the student profile.
All 4 scores display. Level badge displays. CTA navigates to dashboard. Dashboard no longer shows gate on subsequent sessions.

Every API call in the diagnostic flow must handle network errors and non-200 responses gracefully. Show an error state with a 'Try again' button. Do not lose the student's answers — keep them in local state so they do not have to re-answer. Log errors to console for debugging.
Simulated API failure shows error state with retry. Answers are preserved in state across the retry. No blank or frozen screens on error.

On Speaking result, display the transcript returned by the API in a read-only text block below the band scores. Label it clearly: 'What we heard'. Style it as a muted blockquote. This helps the student understand their score and builds trust in the AI.
Transcript renders below the 4 sub-scores. Text is readable and labelled. No truncation — show full transcript.

If a student closes the app mid-diagnostic, their progress must be recoverable. On app load, check the diagnostic status API. If any sections are already scored, resume from the next unscored section. Do not restart from scratch.
Student who completes Listening and closes app resumes at the Reading section, not from the gate. Interim scores for completed sections are displayed.

Listening: audio player tracks remaining time in the clip and shows a progress bar. Reading: soft 5-minute countdown is shown but does not force submission. Both sections show elapsed time. Consider adding a gentle visual cue (amber timer) at 1 minute remaining for Reading.
Listening audio progress bar matches audio duration. Reading timer counts down from 5:00. Neither timer forces submit.

Display the 4 Speaking sub-scores (Fluency & Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range, Pronunciation) as a simple 4-row table with band value per row. Include a one-line label indicating which is the strongest and which needs the most work.
4 sub-scores display in table. Weakest sub-score row highlighted in amber. Strongest sub-score row highlighted in teal.

Who to go to for what
Use Datasets Shared by Paul from Huggingface
API endpoint not responding / returning unexpected shape: Sarthak's problem, not yours.
Design decisions on layout, colours, spacing: make a sensible call and show Paul at the daily check-in.
Browser MediaRecorder API issues (audio recording): this is a known tricky area. Test on Chrome first. Safari has restrictions — flag to Paul early if Safari recording breaks.
Safari audio recording — MediaRecorder may not support webm on iOS/Safari. Test early and flag immediately.

AI scoring latency — Writing may take 10 seconds, Speaking may take 20 seconds. Design the loading states to be informative, not just a spinner. Use messages like 'AI examiner is reviewing your response...'

Supabase realtime vs polling — if Supabase realtime subscriptions are not yet set up, use the polling approach (GET /api/diagnostic/status every 2 seconds). Confirm with Sarthak which approach the backend supports.
